newsitem.title: USA: USDA unveils meat export report proposal.
newsitem.headline: USDA unveils meat export report proposal.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Thursday unveiled a proposal to require reporting of export sales of meat and meat products, including poultry.

Under the proposal, which was published in the Federal Register, firms involved in exporting meat products would be required to report on a weekly basis quantities sold to foreign buyers, the marketing year of the shipment and the country of destination.
The proposal is modelled after the department's export sales reporting rules for grains and oilseeds and would not include prices.
USDA said the proposed reporting week would be Friday through Thursday. The marketing year would be January 1 to December 31.

In its advance notice of proposed rulemaking, USDA said among the questions that would have to be addressed would be the units of measure to be used, the specific products to be included, whether reporting should be separate for fresh/chilled versus frozen product, and the extent of the breakdowns for individual meat cuts and USDA grades.
It said comments must be received by Jan. 13 to be assured consideration.
USDA said it is seeking public comments on the benefits, costs, and methods of collecting meat export sales information.
It said alternative approaches, such as voluntary reporting, would be considered if public feedback indicated substantial problems or concerns with mandatory reporting.

"Although we believe such data would contribute to fairness and efficiency within these markets, we will carefully review all comments and views before we move ahead with any new rule," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement.

The proposal to require meat exporters to report sales activity stems from recommendations by USDA's advisory committee on concentration in agriculture and is aimed at increasing information in the livestock markets.

USDA said between 75 and 125 private firms might be regularly involved in the sale of meat for export and noted many of these firms were small businesses. It estimated the annual paperwork burden for these companies would be about 7,000 hours. USDA said it would cost the government about $400,000 annually to issue the new report.

Export markets account for a rapidly increasing share of U.S. beef, pork, and poultry production. In 1996, exports are forecast to account for 8 percent of beef production, 6 percent of pork production, and 17 percent of poultry production and are seen increasing further in 1997, USDA said.
Total 1995 exports of red meats and poultry meats exceeded $6 billion and generated a trade surplus of nearly $4 billion.
By comparison, in the mid 1980s, less than two percent of annual production of beef and pork, and less than four percent of poultry meat, was exported, USDA said.
